Yes, "pled" is a correct past tense of "plead," though the picture is nuanced depending on context and authority. Both "pleaded" and "pled" are accepted as valid past tense forms in modern English [d1][d2], and the form "pled" actually dates back to the 1200s, nearly as old as "pleaded" itself [d3]. Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary and American Heritage both list "pleaded or pled" as acceptable options, while Webster's New World College Dictionary and the AP Stylebook prefer only "pleaded," calling "pled" colloquial [d5]. In formal and legal writing, "pleaded" is strongly preferred by usage authorities such as Bryan Garner and LawProse, who describe "pleaded" as "unimpeachably correct" and "pled" as defensible only on grounds of common usage [d6][d3]. For everyday writing, most sources agree either form is acceptable, though "pleaded" is the safer choice in professional or legal contexts [d4][d5].
